Putting Seagrass on the Map

📅 2026-07-16 ✍️ Stacy Baez, The Pew Charitable Trusts 🏷️ seagrass mapping, LaSMMI, Western Indian Ocean, marine conservation, blue carbon, Seychelles, coastal ecosystems
🔗 Read the source article →

💡 Quick summary

A regional collaboration across five Western Indian Ocean countries is mapping seagrass ecosystems to create the verified baseline data governments need to protect these critical blue carbon habitats.

📌 Key takeaways

  • Seagrass covers less than 1% of the ocean floor but stores approximately 10% of carbon buried in the ocean annually
  • The LaSMMI initiative is active in Kenya, Madagascar, Mozambique, Tanzania, and Zanzibar
  • A lack of field-verified seagrass maps has hindered conservation efforts and climate commitments
  • Seychelles pioneered the approach, mapping ~160,000 hectares of seagrass and committing to protect 100% by 2030
  • The initiative brings together local research institutions, University of Southampton, WIOMSA, and Pew
